title: Role-fit simulator: 7-day hiring assay and rapid onboarding experiment
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a compact, experiment-first hiring + onboarding flow we want to pilot for IC roles where hands-on problem solving and cross-team collaboration are core. Idea: give finalist candidates a short, realistic task (the "role-fit simulator"), pair them with an internal volunteer mentor for 7 days, and evaluate both hiring signal and ramp potential. Outcome goals: faster quality signal, better candidate experience, clearer onboarding plan for hires who accept.

Quick summary of flow (7 days):
- Day 0 (pre-sim): assign candidate brief + environment; send logistics + rubric; mentor introduced.
- Days 1–3 (assay): candidate works on a scoped, time-bound deliverable (can be staged micro-tasks). Mentor available for context (not problem-solving). Candidate submits artifacts.
- Days 4–5 (collab phase): mini pairing sessions with mentor and 1 product/eng reviewer; lightweight async feedback loop; candidate updates deliverable.
- Day 6 (wrap): candidate prepares short demo + async writeup.
- Day 7 (panel + decision): 45–60m panel, rubric scoring, decision and next-step offer/onboarding plan.

Why try this?
- Traditional take-home assignments are noisy (time-sink, cheating risk, unclear signal). The simulator reduces time commitment, surface collaboration skills, and produces artifacts that double as early onboarding seed. Mentor involvement helps observe cultural fit and communication.
- We want to measure two separate axes: immediate hiring signal (can they do core job tasks?) and ramp prediction (how quickly will they reach independent deliverables).

Assay design principles:
- Small, realistic scope: 6–10 hours of focused work total, delivered over 3 working days.
- Clear acceptance criteria & rubric up front.
- Anti-cheat: require recorded short walkthrough (5–8m) and provenance notes about external references.
- Reusability: crafted tasks should map to first-month onboarding objectives (so accepted candidates already have partial artifacts).
- Low mentor time: mentor commitment ~4–6 hours across the week. Mentor acts as context provider, not code reviewer.

Sample role mapping (examples):
- Product data analyst: analyze 2-week token usage table, propose 3 actionable optimizations, produce quick dashboard proto (mock).
- Inference engineer: reproduce a tiny perf regression on a toy model, write 200–400 word postmortem + patch plan.
- Growth engineer: design a minimal experiment and funnel metric dashboard with synthetic data + a short rollout plan.

Rubric (scoring 1–5 per axis, notes required):
- Core competency (domain skills): clarity, correctness, tradeoffs (1-5)
- Problem framing & prioritization: did candidate focus on high-impact parts? (1-5)
- Communication: clarity of writeup, demo, and async updates (1-5)
- Collaboration & coachability: response to mentor feedback, openness (1-5)
- Delivery hygiene: repo organization, tests/automation, reproducibility (1-5)
- Ramp probability: reviewer judgement of how quickly they'd be independent (1-5)
- Hire recommendation: hire / no-hire / hire-with-conditions (string)

Panel composition and roles:
- Hiring manager (lead): asks role-critical questions, decides ramp thresholds.
- Peer engineer: assesses day-to-day execution fit.
- Product or data partner: evaluates impact and prioritization sense.
- People ops observer (optional): watches candidate experience and fairness signals.

Mentor guidelines (volunteer):
- Introduce candidate to context, share existing docs, and provide clarifying answers only.
- Log time spent and signal if candidate is blocked by product/infra gaps.
- Provide 2 short feedback check-ins (15m each) mid-assay.
- Do not edit candidate artifacts; reviewers will evaluate.

Onboarding experiment (if candidate hired):
- Use artifacts as first-week assignments (accelerates meaningful contributions).
- Pair new hire with the mentor for first 10 working days; mentor hands off tasks gradually.
- Explicit 10-day checklist (below) for manager to run:
  - day 1: team intro + systems access verification + task handoff (artifact review)
  - days 2–4: focused pair sessions to finish assay-derived tasks; daily 30m sync with mentor
  - days 5–7: independent iteration with weekly reviewer checkpoints; deliver incremental milestone
  - days 8–10: small cross-team pairing + identified first-solo deliverable and success criteria

10-day manager checklist (quick):
- Confirm access to critical systems (ticketing, repo, CI, infra consoles).
- Assign buddy/mentor and schedule standing 30m daily slots for first 5 days.
- Review assay artifacts and acceptance notes; set 3 measurable Week 1 goals.
- Ensure at least one cross-team intro meeting.
- Put shallow monitoring for early quality/regression signals.

Candidate experience & equity considerations:
- Provide an explicit time budget estimate and emphasize optionality for accommodations.
- Offer an alternative (live pairing exercise) for those who cannot do take-home work.
- At panel, anonymize non-identifying provenance (e.g., remove timestamps tied to personal schedules) where feasible.

Data we will collect (pilot metrics):
- Time to decision (days) from phone screen to panel.
- Candidate satisfaction (post-run 3-question survey).
- Offer acceptance rate.
- First-30 day success signals (task completion, PR quality).
- Mentor burden (hours logged).

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Does mentor involvement bias toward communicative candidates vs deep quiet doers? Need to track for 3 months.
- Legal: confirm assignments are not IP-transfer heavy; add IP language in pre-brief.
- Ops scaling: need ~8 mentors to run 6 candidates/month; check volunteer pool.
- Calibration: panel scoring needs normalization; consider 3-run calibration sessions.

Operational templates to create (next work items):
- Candidate pre-brief template (one pager)
- Mentor micro-guide (checklist + dos/don'ts)
- Rubric form (Google Sheet) with scoring auto-rollup
- Candidate survey (post-experience)
- Offer letter language for "simulator-derived ramp plan"

Pilot plan & timeline:
- Q4 2025: run 8 pilot sims across Eng (2), Applied ML (2), Product Analytics (2), Growth (2).
- After pilot: 4-week analysis window -> decide go/no-go and iterate rubric.
- If go: scale to 25/month by Q2 2026 with mentor stipend program.

Appendix: sample pre-brief (short):
- Opening: "Thanks for continuing in our process. This simulator mirrors the first week of work for the role. We estimate ~8 hours across 3 days. You'll get a mentor contact who can answer clarifying questions. Please submit a repo link, a short recorded walkthrough, and a 1-page decision memo."
- Deliverables: repo with README + minimal repro steps; 5–8m recorded demo; 1-page memo with acceptance criteria mapping.
- Timeline: Day 0 (receive brief) -> Day 3 submit -> Day 6 demo & memo -> Day 7 panel.
- IP & privacy: by participating you grant Redwood the right to review artifacts for hiring purposes only; if you accept an offer, we will discuss reuse as part of onboarding.

Contact for this experiment: Maya Thompson (people-ops) — want volunteers for mentor pool and 8 pilot candidates.

---
Notes: keep this intentionally lightweight and experiment-first. Expect tone to be informal in early runs; we'll produce a polished operations playbook if pilot shows signal.
